headline: Sequence foundation models are tested for hidden shortcuts such as ligand invariance and reading-frame reliance
label: Sequence Model Reliability Audits
summary: New preprints pair modality-specific pretraining with audits showing models ignoring ligand identity or relying on reading-frame cues absent from splicing machinery.
synthesis: Several items extend pretrained sequence representations to new tasks: IsoAlign uses JEPA objectives for isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment, PDLMs jointly model paired protein-DNA sequences, PALM adapts ESM2 with LoRA and BiLSTM, and MaskNGly predicts N-glycosylation zero-shot from embeddings, matching supervised predictors. The more consequential results concern failure modes. On MET kinase deep mutational scans across 11 inhibitors, models are largely ligand-invariant. Black-box neural splice-site predictors depend on reading-frame-altering mutations and miss poison exons, unlike grey-box models. The RNA-small molecule survey organizes evaluation by binding site, preference, and pose tasks. The common thread is that benchmark performance needs mechanism-aware, task-stratified validation, not just stronger pretraining.
